correctness.rationale: An interior zero edge needs its predecessor and successor bits to sum to one; a terminal zero instead adds the number of selected edges at its degree-three endpoint to its one interior neighbor. These give exactly the displayed pair transfer and endpoint tests. At length two the identity matrix forces (f,h)=(p,g), so the same boundary formula neither misses nor duplicates any bit words. For a labeled cycle the trace counts each cyclic bit assignment at its fixed starting index once. Direct multiplication yields T^4=T^3+T, hence the same recurrence for the theta count and the comparator as any length at least six is reduced by one or three. A separate endpoint-sharing subset enumeration reproduced all twenty unordered base rows and the corresponding cycles. The only zero difference in the base is 222 (6 vs 6); neither predecessor outside the base can be 222, so strong induction gives strict positivity elsewhere.
residual_risks: Only simple three-path theta graphs with all lengths at least two, and all PED sets, not minimum sets or dominating induced matchings. The finite enumeration verifies the base, not the infinite theorem by itself.

The same local transfer recurrence was previously used for lollipops. Neither comparison gives the all-length theta-versus-cycle bound with its K2,3 equality case; originality credit is for that family-specific comparison and the two-terminal specialization, not for the matrix, cycle sequence, or existence of a counting algorithm.

value.rationale: Settles a natural infinite bicyclic family in the connected-graph cycle-comparator conjecture and identifies an exceptional equality missed by a generic counting algorithm. The shared recurrence gives a structural explanation for why a finite comparison establishes the full family, rather than a collection of numerical instances.
residual_risks: No conclusion about other bicyclic graphs, more paths or the general conjecture.
